claim_scope: Exact local platform-validation topology security only. No repository workflow, real migration, application runner, database persistence, dashboard, recovery, clean-clone, or release claim is included.

checks.result: Revision 1, its normalized render, contract lock, and the failed U04 implementation lock remain archived byte-for-byte. Revision 2 adds only an exact-base copy-only database image and a new ownership-seeded volume path.
All 14 contract mutations failed closed, including direct database-base use and the prior unseeded mount path.
All 14 real implementation mutations failed closed, including UID/GID ownership-seed drift. No mutation built an image or started a container.
Four exact-base images built with BuildKit network none, pull disabled, no cache, locked frontend, contract labels, numeric users, and exact local image IDs recorded in the runtime lock.
The ownership-seeded named volume initialized PostgreSQL and reached healthy while the container ran as 70:70 with a read-only root.
Database, migration, Python, and Node containers used the four exact runtime-lock image IDs and required numeric users.
All four containers were non-privileged, read-only-root, cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges, unpublished, and attached only to the internal data bridge, with no Docker endpoint mount.

Fixed Python and Node probes denied root and staged-input writes, allowed only staged-output writes, denied external egress, exposed no sensitive environment name, and found no Docker or Podman endpoint.
A second host-CLI invocation verified and reused all four image IDs, resumed the exact labeled volume, repeated every hardening probe, and passed.
Both successful invocations removed every IncidentSeal container and the internal network. The exact labeled database volume remains retained by policy.

retained_attempts.note: Two pre-remediation runtime attempts remain distinct and retained; neither is rewritten as a pass. The original failed volume remains retained and was not reused by revision 2.

The first revision-2 static implementation attempt found a generated Python __pycache__ byte inside the exact build context. The validator rejected it before any build, and the cache was moved intact to recoverable non-OneDrive temp custody before the passing replay.
